opportunities.amount: Up to $1,000,000 in non-dilutive cash prizes across the competition: $5,000 to each of up to 50 semifinalists, a further $20,000 to each of up to 20 finalists, then $200,000 / $100,000 / $50,000 to first, second and third. opportunities.summary: BEST LIVE ITEM ON THE BOARD, and the deadline is 19 Oct at 5pm ET. It is an OPEN-TOPIC competition — you are not fitting a product to a stated problem — and one of the four named priority portfolios is 'Immersive and Wearables: smart electronic devices that can be worn by or attached to the user to gather data or provide insight', which is Vybe's category described by the Army in its own words. Four rounds: white paper by 19 Oct, virtual semifinal pitch 18-29 Jan 2027, finals at eMerge Americas in Miami 2-4 Mar 2027, then the SBIR/STTR window to 30 Apr. THE ONE GATE TO READ CAREFULLY: technologies falling EXCLUSIVELY within the U.S. Army Medical Research and Development Command portfolio — military operational medicine, clinical and rehabilitative medicine, infectious disease, CBRN — are excluded. Vybe's honest position is a commercial consumer wearable with a dual-use readiness application, not a medical technology, which is both true and the only framing that clears this exclusion. Do not describe it as a medical or diagnostic capability to sound more serious; that is the sentence that makes it ineligible. Judges compare unlike technologies, so the published evaluation emphasis is commercial traction, a defensible technical advantage, a direct line to an Army need, and a credible transition path.

Eligibility is the same test Vybe already passed for xTech|Search 10, and the 26.BX solicitation family is literally the one xTech's follow-on topic sits in. Open the Release 6 topic list on DSIP first and decide that before drafting anything. If nothing fits, the thing to wait for is an OPEN TOPIC cycle, which takes any dual-use technology — none is open as of today, and the published schedule shows only Specific Topics and Strategic Breakthrough, the latter needing a prior Phase II. Note Phase I is a three-month feasibility study with a structured curriculum and a kickoff meeting, and it does NOT require an existing DAF customer: finding one is part of the work. Letters of support from government personnel are not required but are read.

Independent contractors and 1099 workers do not count, and an employer exempt from those reporting requirements is not eligible at all. One application per federal tax ID per period. Training must come from a provider on Ohio's eligible list, and that provider must be independent of the employer.
